id.description: id is the line to change.

description.description: description is shown to employees as the task description once picked.

date.description: date is the day being recorded, as YYYY-MM-DD.

employee_id.description: employee_id records the day on someone else's behalf.

end_time.description: end_time is the local end as HH:MM.

start_time.description: start_time is the local start as HH:MM.

timezone.description: timezone is the IANA zone of the person recording it.

work_mode.description: work_mode is one of onsite, remote or hybrid.

flow.time.v1.WorkDay.description:
WorkDay is one person's working day: the mode, the clock, and the state of its
approval. The individual pieces of work are its lines.

approved_at.description: approved_at is when it was approved.

approved_by.description: approved_by is the approver, once the day has been approved.

break_minutes.description: break_minutes is unpaid break time, subtracted from the clocked total.

clocked_minutes.description: clocked_minutes is end minus start minus breaks, or zero when unclocked.

created_at.description: created_at is when the record was created.

date.description: date is the calendar day in the person's own timezone, as YYYY-MM-DD.

employee_id.description: employee_id is the person the day belongs to.

end_time.description: end_time is the local end of the day as HH:MM.

gap_minutes.description:
gap_minutes is clocked minus logged. It is reported, never enforced: a
blocked submission produces invented lines rather than honest ones.

id.description: id is the unique identifier for the resource.

logged_by.description:
logged_by is the user who recorded the day, which differs from employee_id
when a manager fills it in on someone's behalf.

logged_minutes.description: logged_minutes is the sum of this day's lines.

reopened_at.description: reopened_at is when it was reopened.

reopened_by.description: reopened_by is the manager who reopened an approved day.

start_time.description:
start_time is the local start of the day as HH:MM, or null for a day that
records only its lines.

status.description: status is one of draft, submitted, approved, rejected or reopened.

timezone.description:
timezone is the IANA zone the day was recorded in. Stored per record because
a travelling worker's day boundary is their own, not the workspace's.

updated_at.description: updated_at is when the record was last changed.

user_id.description:
user_id is the employee's auth user id, populated when the caller already
resolved it (the team view, which joins against workspace membership).
Callers reading their own day already know their own identity and get
this unset.

work_mode.description:
work_mode is one of onsite, remote or hybrid. It is the day's default and a
line may override it.

flow.time.v1.WorkDayLine.description:
WorkDayLine is one piece of work inside a day. It is persisted as an HR time
entry, so payroll and Flow read the same rows.

client_key.description:
client_key is generated by the client before the line is sent. It makes an
offline retry idempotent, so a field worker syncing twice does not log twice.

created_at.description: created_at is when the record was created.

id.description: id is the unique identifier for the resource.

is_billable.description: is_billable marks the line as chargeable, defaulted from the work type.

logged_by.description: logged_by is who recorded the line.

project_id.description:
project_id is the project the work was for. A line may have a project and no
task, for work that is not tracked as one.

status.description: status mirrors the day's approval state for this line.

task_id.description: task_id is the task the work was for.

updated_at.description: updated_at is when the record was last changed.

work_day_id.description: work_day_id is the day this line belongs to.

work_mode.description: work_mode overrides the day's mode for this line only. Null means inherit.

work_type_id.description: work_type_id is the classification node, at either level of the tree.

flow.time.v1.WorkType.description:
WorkType is one node of the two-level work classification a workspace admin
maintains, for example Development with a Code review child. Entries point at
either level; hr_category_id maps the node onto HR's payroll category so one
entry serves both project reporting and payroll.

archived.description: archived hides the node from pickers without breaking historic entries.

created_at.description: created_at is when the record was created.

description.description:
description is a business-authored explanation of what this work type
covers, shown to employees as a read-only "Task Description" once they
pick the type in Log Hours - distinct from the free-text description an
employee types for what they actually did.

hr_category_id.description: hr_category_id maps this node to an HR payroll category.

id.description: id is the unique identifier for the resource.

name.description: name is the display name of this work type.

parent_id.description:
parent_id is the parent node, or null for a top-level type. The tree is
exactly two levels deep.

sort_order.description: sort_order controls the order the tree is presented in.
